svg.title: Client / Server Integration Pilot: Setup and Asynchronous Request/Reply

g.text: Client / Server Integration Pilot: Setup and Asynchronous Request/Reply
OS-independent public API view; IPC arrows are transport messages, not C++ method calls.
Client/server objects have been created through IClientFactory/IServerFactory with matching protocol configuration.
One permitted interleaving is shown; callback completion is not guaranteed to happen after an API call returns.
Pilot configuration: sync_first_connect = false, truly_async = true,
max_async_replies >= 1, max_queued_sends >= 1; one request, non-empty callbacks.
This pilot uses UserData containing a context pointer.
Returning a unique_ptr<IConnectionHandler> instead selects its methods
in place of the non-connect server callbacks; that alternative is not shown.
Nested in Start(), on the calling thread.
The callback may call Stop(); this scenario continues without stopping.
The library owns connection; the callback receives an IServerConnection&.
UserData is associated with the accepted connection, not returned to the client.
Ready follows return from the Starting callback.
Ready's thread is unspecified; it may precede return from Start().
No request accepted and no reply_callback invocation for this call.
Success means accepted, not delivered or replied to.
Returning before completion is the interleaving shown, not a guarantee.
Returning success from sent_with_reply_callback does not send a reply.
Reply() is a separate call on connection, shown inside the callback here.
A valid-size reply and successful delivery are assumed in this branch.
[Background send fails or peer disconnects before a reply]
Error is reported by reply_callback, not by the earlier successful return.
Connection loss also produces Stopping/Stopped state callbacks (not expanded here);
a background send failure need not stop the connection.
Client callback threads are unspecified except where stated.
Start() callback captures must remain alive until kStopped;
reply_callback captures must survive completion. Teardown is not shown.
Server callbacks for one session are serialized; their threads are unspecified.
Server-callback captures must remain alive until StopListening() returns.
StopListening() must not be called from a server callback.
